title: Transfer test: subexponential #k-SAT technique (openai/math family 378) to ECDLP
question: Does the sparse-polynomial common-zero counting / shared-linear-summary technique of 'The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False' (openai/math family 378) give any ECDLP algorithm beating Pollard rho, directly via CNF encoding or via the summation-polynomial decomposition step?
rationale: External, Lean-formalized (per its own catalogue) subexponential counting algorithm; our SAT and index-calculus routes failed at the polynomial-system step. PI note: direct CNF encoding has n >= circuit size >> log r variables, so the headline theorem cannot beat rho; only the technique might.
success_criteria: Exact statements; reproducible evidence; honest negatives.
resource_limit: One bounded subagent; no recursion; no commits.
